notes: Source 4 = Finkelstein 1990a, Eretz-Israel 21 (Hebrew); quotes are from the packet's English translation. The article is about the Dhahr Mirzbaneh spur, north of Kh. Samiyye. It describes no pool, pit or grave at Kh. Samiyye itself, which is named only in the introduction ('not founded before the Roman period'). The features are the surrounding shaft-tomb cemeteries, all within 2 km. Grid assignments: s4f1 = WBADB S1644 (Dhahr Mirzbaneh, the excavated site). s4f2-s4f3 = S1647 ('Hundreds of shaft tombs in several concentrations. Previously excavated by Lapp', citing Finkelstein 1990a): one point for the Mirzbaneh concentrations. s4f5 = S1676 ('Ein Samiya cemetery with the silver cup; Yeivin, Dever), the same cemetery as the 1970 excavation 'near Khirbet Samiya'. s4f7 = S1683 (c. 40 shaft tombs, citing Finkelstein 1990a, beside el-Qasr S1684). Cemetery 7 (s4f6, c. 60 tombs) may be WBADB S1666/E219 ('about 60 tombs'), but the place is not clearly the same, so its position is none. s4f4 is placed only relative to the spur. Not coded: the tumulus, which is 'perhaps' the tomb of an important person (speculative); the 'Ein Samiya spring (not a pool); cupmarks. No plan position: Fig. 1 has no north arrow, and Figs. 4, 5 and 7 do not show Kh. Samiyye.
